redFirst.basis: `python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__filed_returns.py --selftest` in a throwaway tree at HEAD exited 1 with 3 of 93 collected tests failing an assertion, the task's own among them (named by --case, HEAD's own tests green on HEAD's code), each passing with the working tree's implementation - ds1 (house FAIL): SELFTEST FAILED: 90/93 cases passed; run without CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, OLDPWD; dependencies linked from the project root, entry by entry as symlinks: node_modules - .cache, .vite, .vite-temp are not linked and a new entry a runner makes beside the links stays in the throwaway, but a write into a linked entry lands in the project's own node_modules and is not watched; no .npmrc to carry or drop

outcome.technical: PRODUCT NOT AFFECTED; the fault was the test fixture alone. Established on POSIX: sha256 of json.dumps(_executor())+'\n' is d769a8... with LF bytes and 0c1436... with CRLF bytes - exactly the row and file digests CI windows-latest printed for rj8. In _journaled_cases the return is written by M.file_once (newline='', so LF bytes; the row digest is over those), then rewritten with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') in text mode before rj8, which on Windows writes CRLF, so the checked read was RIGHT to refuse. Product path traced end to end: audit-task.py file-return -> _filed_returns.file_once writes with newline='' (no translation, writes exactly the text it was given); drive-phase._journal_filed_return -> _journal_io.append_from_cli_why -> the append sets row stateHash = _journal_io.file_hash(target), which opens 'rb' over the bytes on disk after the write; read_filed_return_checked -> filed_digest_problem -> return_digest opens 'rb'. Every digest is over the on-disk bytes, none over text; .gitattributes '* text=auto eol=lf' keeps a checkout from translating committed returns. No product step sees translated bytes on Windows. Changes: (1) plugins/audit/tests/test__filed_returns.py: the rj4 and rj8 fixture rewrites now use newline='' as file_once does; new rc-block case rc1 writes a return with explicit CRLF bytes through file_once, appends the real task.return.filed row through _journal_io.append_from_cli_why, reads it back with read_all, asserts the row digest equals return_digest and differs from the digest over the untranslated (LF) text, the checked read is clean with no unchecked note, and after the CRLF bytes become LF (same JSON) the read is refused naming both digests; new ds-block cases ds1 (the filing site set is exactly return_digest in _filed_returns, file_hash in _journal_io, none in drive-phase; the row's stateHash is assigned only from file_hash or None; the two functions' try bodies are one AST; filed_digest_problem compares via return_digest), ds2 (a second site hashing text-mode-read text is reported by name), ds2a allow twin (hashing handed text, or opening without hashing, is no site). (2) plugins/audit/scripts/manifest/_filed_returns.py: new file_digest_sites(source) with _opens_for_reading/_calls_sha256 - the AST reader the source check uses; takes an argument and walks no tree, so it is not a gate. The digest is still two byte-identical function bodies in two layer-mates (_journal_io and _filed_returns may not import each other); literally one function would need a shared lower module such as _machine_paths.py plus _journal_io.py, both outside this task's files, and was not owed since the product is unaffected - ds1 holds the two to one AST body instead. drive-phase.py and test_drive_phase.py unchanged. Mutation checks in a scratch copy (never the shared tree): return_digest hashing text-mode-read text turns rc1 and ds1 red with every LF case green (91/93); the old fixture's translation simulated on POSIX turns rj8 red with exactly 'carries sha256:d769a8 and it now hashes to sha256:0c1436'. Runs: python3 plugins/audit/tests/test__filed_returns.py --selftest red first at 90/93 (ds1, ds2, ds2a, file_digest_sites absent), then 93/93 exit 0; python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py exit 0, 335/335 files ok; ruff and vermin on the two files clean.
outcome.descriptive: The rj8 Windows red was the fixture rewriting a return in text mode; the product hashes on-disk bytes throughout, and a CRLF case plus a one-digest source check now hold that on POSIX.
